title: Platform team wiki: systems & services, runbooks, dashboards, roadmap (Q1 2026 retrospective)
author: Priya Singh
content:
Overview

This document is the canonical platform team wiki page that consolidates: systems & services inventory; dashboards and alerts guidance; prioritized runbooks; a short retrospective for Q1 2026; and the near-term roadmap. It is intended for on-call engineers, platform owners, and cross-functional stakeholders (SRE, infra, product).

Sections (quick links)
1. Systems & services inventory
2. Operating SLOs and alert matrix
3. Dashboards and alerting playbook
4. Runbooks (incident + maintenance)
5. How-tos (common ops tasks)
6. Q1 2026 retrospective + action items
7. Roadmap (Q2-Q4 2026)
8. Ownership, escalation, and runbook templates

1) Systems & services inventory (scope)
Purpose: Provide a concise inventory of the platform services we operate and the primary contact/owner for each service. Use this as the source of truth for runbook linkage and dashboard mapping.

Service | Description | Primary owner | Pager | Key dashboards
--- | --- | --- | --- | ---
control-plane | API gateway + routing + auth for hosted inference | Platform Services (team) | oncall-platform | /dashboards/control-plane-overview
serving-runtime | GPU inference fleet, scheduler, KV cache | Serving Runtime | oncall-serving | /dashboards/serving-runtime-health
data-cache | Redis prefix cache for KV and shared metadata | Eng Infra | oncall-infra | /dashboards/data-cache-metrics
billing-worker | Usage collection and billing pipeline | FinOps | oncall-finops | /dashboards/billing-pipeline

Note: For each service above, there is a dedicated runbook link later in this page. Inventory ownership should be reviewed monthly by the platform manager.

2) Operating SLOs and alert matrix
Short version: SLOs are service-level; alert thresholds are derived from SLO burn rates and operational capacity. Critical SLOs we track: 99th percentile tail latency for control-plane (<= 300ms for small requests), P99 serving inference latency per model class, request success rate >= 99.95 (per region).

Example SLO/Alert table
SLO | Target | Primary alert | Severity | Pager
--- | ---:| --- | --- | ---
Control-plane P99 latency | 300ms | control-plane-p99>300ms for 5m | Sev2 | oncall-platform
Serving runtime P99 token latency | model-class A: 120ms | serving-runtime-p99>120ms for 5m | Sev2 | oncall-serving
Request success rate | 99.95% (1h) | control-plane-error-rate>0.05% for 1h | Sev1 | oncall-platform
KV cache miss rate | <5% | data-cache-miss>8% for 10m | Sev2 | oncall-infra
Billing ingestion lag | <2m | billing-lag>10m | Sev2 | oncall-finops

Alerting guidance
- Use Sev1 for customer-impacting, sustained errors or data loss (e.g., request success < 99.8% for 15m).
- Use Sev2 for degraded performance that affects latencies or throughput but does not cause broad errors.
- All Sev1 pages require an incident leader assignment within 5 minutes and a postmortem within 72 hours if the event meets the postmortem criteria.

3) Dashboards and alerting playbook
Dashboard conventions
- Each dashboard must include: Summary row (SLOs), P90/P99 latency, error rate, request volume, and top two dimensioned breakdowns (region, model-type).
- Use consistent naming: /dashboards/<service>-overview, /dashboards/<service>-latency, /dashboards/<service>-capacity.
- Time ranges default to last 1h, 6h, 24h views.

Recommended dashboard list (links internal)
- /dashboards/control-plane-overview — API traffic, auth errors, route-level latencies.
- /dashboards/serving-runtime-health — GPU utilization, KV cache hit/miss, queue depth, per-worker latencies.
- /dashboards/cost-and-efficiency — batching stats, token throughput, per-model cost.
- /dashboards/billing-pipeline — ingestion lag, message backlog, processing errors.

Alert escalation flow (summary)
1. Alert fires -> page -> assigned on-call.
2. On-call triages using the runbook linked in the page.
3. If not resolved in escalation_ttl (15m for Sev1, 60m for Sev2), escalate to secondary and Engineering Manager.
4. For Sev1 incidents, create an incident channel and notify stakeholders (PM, Eng Manager, Product Ops).

4) Runbooks (incident + maintenance)
Generic incident runbook (template)
1. Detect and Triage
  - Confirm alert: reproduce or validate metrics. Check dashboards: /dashboards/<service>-overview.
  - Identify scope: region(s), percentage of traffic affected, model classes.
2. Mitigate
  - Apply known mitigations (see service-specific runbook below). Common mitigations: rollback recent deploy, scale up replica pool, redirect traffic to degraded model tier, enable degraded caching.
3. Communicate
  - Post summary to incident channel: \"Incident [ID]: symptom, impact, mitigation steps taken, next steps\".
4. Remediate & Restore
  - Execute root-cause fixes or stable rollback. Monitor until SLOs restored for 30m.
5. Close & Postmortem
  - If incident meets threshold (customer impact > 30min or SEV1), assign postmortem owner and schedule within 72 hours.

Service-specific excerpt: serving-runtime 
- Common causes: kernel OOM on orthogonal models, slow KV cache responses, GPU preemption.
Quick mitigations:
- Scale: `kubectl -n serving scale deployment/worker --replicas=<N+2>`
- Redirect: update router rule to fallback model variant: `redwoodctl route set --service serving-runtime --fallback-model small-variant`
- Cache flush (last resort): `redis-cli -h <host> FLUSHDB <prefix>` (use with caution — notify product).

Maintenance runbook (scheduled deploy)
1. Announce maintenance 72h in advance on #platform-announce and update calendar.
2. Run preflight checks: synthetic traffic smoke tests (see smoke test script snippet below).
3. Apply canary to 5% traffic for 10 minutes, verify SLO metrics.
4. Increment rollout by 25% every 10 minutes while monitoring P99 and error rate.
5. If any metric regresses beyond threshold, pause and rollback to previous stable.

Smoke test snippet (CI job)
```
# run a 2m smoke test against control-plane
python infra/tests/smoke_test.py --target control-plane --qps 20 --duration 120
```

5) How-tos (common ops tasks)
How to add a new dashboard
1. Copy the dashboard template: /dashboards/templates/service-overview.json.
2. Replace variables: service, owner, SLO thresholds.
3. Add dimension panels for region and model-type.
4. Submit PR to dashboards repo and request review from observability@redwood.com.

How to tune an alert
1. Confirm baseline by checking historical alert firing rate (30d).
2. Adjust threshold conservatively (10-20% change), set a runbook link, and add muted windows for planned maintenance.
3. Test by triggering a synthetic alert (use `alert-test` job) and verifying runbook execution.

How to add a new service to inventory
1. Create a new entry in this page's inventory table and add the service owner.
2. Create dashboards (overview, latency, capacity) and link them in the inventory.
3. Add alerting rules with initial thresholds and label them `template:needs-tuning` so the on-call can tune after 1 week in production.

6) Q1 2026 retrospective (summary + metrics)
Summary: Q1 saw three Sev1 incidents: two in late Jan (control-plane auth outage, 42m) and one in Feb (billing ingestion backlog, 95m). We increased scheduled capacity for serving-runtime and rolled out KV cache improvements that reduced average token latency by ~12% and reduced P99 spikes 18%.

Quantitative highlights
- Incidents meeting postmortem threshold: 3
- Mean time to acknowledge (MTTA): 4.2 minutes (goal: <5m)
- Mean time to restore (MTTR): 68 minutes (goal: <60m) — improvement area
- SLO burn: control-plane consumed 7% error budget in Q1, serving-runtime consumed 9%

Action items (owner / ETA)
- Implement automatic canary rollback in the control-plane canary pipeline (owner: CI/CD team; ETA: 2026-03-31)
- Improve billing pipeline visibility: add per-shard backlog panel (owner: FinOps; ETA: 2026-04-15)
- Reduce MTTR by automating common mitigations (scale/redirect) with one-click ops in the console (owner: Platform Tools; ETA: 2026-05-30)
- Run quarterly on-call practice game-days focused on KV cache failure modes (owner: SRE; ETA: 2026-04-30)

7) Roadmap (Q2-Q4 2026)
Q2 2026 - Automatic canary rollback and improved telemetry for control-plane
- Per-model-class resource recommendations in Optimize (pilot)
- Runbook automation: one-click mitigations for top 3 incident types

Q3 2026 - Multi-region SLO-aware routing and failover tests
- Observability retention policies and cost controls

Q4 2026 - Private deployment runbook standardization and on-prem smoke harness
- Platform-wide chaos-testing program (stage 1)

8) Ownership, escalation, and runbook templates
- Primary on-call rotation: oncall-platform (rota details in team wiki).
- Secondary escalation: platform-engineering-manager@redwood.com.
- Postmortem owner assignment: incident lead must assign within 24h.

Appendix A: Runbook template (copy/paste)
Title: <service> incident runbook
Symptom: <short description>
Impact: <who/what is affected>
Detection: <alerts/metrics used>
Immediate mitigations: <mitigations to reduce customer impact>
Root cause analysis steps: <investigation checklist>
Long-term action items: <owner + ETA>
